subject: Mutual Action Plan handoff: SE / ML-eng sync for evaluation & close timeline
messages:

To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@cloudlane.io>, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@cloudlane.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan handoff: SE / ML-eng sync for evaluation & close timeline

Hi Alex & Priya,

Thanks again for the productive product review last week. Per our conversation, I wanted to kick off a quick MAP handoff so we can align technical owners, evaluation scope, and a proposed path to close by mid-November. I’ve looped in Dev (Solutions Engineer) and Maya (ML Engineer) from our side — they’ll lead the technical evaluation and address model/latency/cost questions.

High-level proposed MAP (draft):
- Week 1 (this week): technical deep-dive + environment access (SE + customer infra lead)
- Week 2: run targeted evals (latency & throughput, sample prompts), Redwood provides evaluation checklist and baseline scripts
- Week 3: analyze results, iterate on model selection & quantization recommendations
- Week 4: finalize recommended config, procurement/terms review, signoff

What I need from you to lock the MAP:
1) Confirm the customer engineering owner for the technical sessions (I assume Alex will lead)
2) Any security/compliance contacts we should add (SOC2 evidence requests may come up)
3) Target close date — we suggested Nov 15 internally; does that work for CloudLane?

Dev & Maya, quick intro notes for the CloudLane team: Dev will own the infra onboarding, sample runbook, and live demo. Maya will drive evaluation metrics, prompt test harness, and quality regression checks.

I’ve also created a shared MAP doc (link below) where we can track milestones and action items. I’ll wait for Alex/Priya to confirm an initial 60–90 minute technical sync time.

Shared doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcdExampleMAP
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

Thanks — looking forward to getting this going.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
@rachel_kim

Thanks Rachel — sounds good.

I’ll be the engineering owner on our side for the initial sessions; Priya (product ops) will support scheduling and procurement questions. We have a security contact (Samir Dash, samir.dash@cloudlane.io) who should be included if we dive into compliance evidence.

Nov 15 target is realistic for us provided we can complete the technical evals in the next three weeks. For availability: I can do Thu Oct 22 10–11:30am PDT or Fri Oct 23 2–4pm PDT for the first technical sync.

Looking forward to the checklist and the deep-dive from Dev & Maya.

—Alex

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: SE intro + proposed agenda and access items — Redwood eval runbook

Hi Alex — great to meet you virtually. Quick intro: I’m Dev (SE) — I’ll run the infra onboarding, provide the evaluation VM/scripts, and walk through the end-to-end sample request flow during our sync.

Proposed 75-minute agenda for the first sync (we can shorten to 60 if needed):
- 0–10m: Intros & roles (who’s on for data/infra/security)
- 10–30m: Architecture review — where you’d run inference (VPC, cloud region), expected request volume, and network constraints
- 30–55m: Live demo of Redwood eval harness + runthrough of the provided scripts (we’ll execute a couple short runs)
- 55–70m: Data/security/Q&A (including Samir if he joins)
- 70–75m: Next steps & MAP task owners

Pre-reqs / access I’ll need before the session:
1) A short-run service account or scoped API key for a sandbox environment (we can run from our hosted eval if you prefer)
2) Network diagram (high level) and any IP allowlist requirements
3) Approx sample size and concurrency targets (so we can size batch tests)

I uploaded a short evaluation checklist and a baseline run script to the shared doc and attached the PDF here for quick review.

If Oct 22 10am works, I’ll send a calendar invite with a Zoom link.
